classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the descending boundary has horizontal and vertical totals equal to the overall width and height, without finding individual step lengths.

content.prompt: Find the perimeter of the shape below. Once you figure out the trick, look at some of the previous perimeter exercises and see how quickly you can do them!

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14 diagram at the bottom of printed page 273
spec.description: Unshaded closed rectilinear outline with a descending staircase boundary, a long right vertical segment and a short final outward step. Only the left overall height and bottom overall width are labelled. Drawing coordinates reproduce the silhouette and do not supply individual step measurements.
spec.mathematics: Overall height 10 m and overall width 16 m. Every segment on the upper/right boundary travels right or down, so its horizontal lengths total 16 m and its vertical lengths total 10 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied labels 10 m and 16 m are visible; no perimeter or inferred side lengths appear.

inlines.text: The descending boundary has total horizontal length 16 m and total vertical length 10 m.

answer.worked:
All the rightward segments together span $16\ \mathrm{m}$, and all the downward segments together span $10\ \mathrm{m}$. Add these to the bottom and left sides.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Perimeter}&=16+10+16+10\\\text{Perimeter}&=52\ \mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$
